as_extracts.name: LFREF102-E13
as_extracts.description: Students explore and recognise the influence of culture on language and identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2E04 - French
content_descriptions.text: explore connections between language and culture through play and/or imagination
content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with French Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures, facial expressions and body language through games such as charades, or by incorporating them into stories, plays or songs to enhance meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing simple French games that are similar to Australian ones (e.g. à la déli-delo, le fermier dans son pré), and/or playing traditional outdoor French children’s games (e.g. 1, 2, 3 soleil; cache-cache; la marelle; le jeu de l’escargot)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing and engaging with cultural items from French-speaking countries, such as Euros, postcards and authentic items

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging ideas, feelings and understandings of language and culture through play-based experiences such as dress-ups, puppets, and pretend cafés and French shops such as la boulangerie and le marché

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that different kinds of language (including spoken and body language) are used in different situations with different people, for example, observing exchanges between children and parents (e.g. Un bisou, Papa ! Je t’aime chéri(e).) and exchanges with unfamiliar adults (e.g. Bonjour Madame, comment allez-vous ?)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing gestures to convey different messages, such as indicating that they think someone is not telling the truth by pointing to their own eye and saying Mon oeil !, for example, playing the game ‘2 truths and a lie’, using a simple structure such as name, age and favourite colour

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected to culture, such as eating pancakes on Mardi Gras or making la bûche de Noël for Christmas

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2U05 - French
content_descriptions.text: reflect on how language, culture and identity are interconnected and discuss how French-speaking communities are similar to or different from others
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing their own use of words, expressions or behaviours that make them who they are, including words from different languages known to the class and ways of celebrating or talking that may not be familiar to other people

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a short video and noticing formalities in French-speaking communities such as handshakes, la bise or standing up to greet a visitor to the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a French children’s book about school and family life, and comparing aspects of Australian and French children’s lifestyles, such as school canteen meals or daily greetings between family members or friends

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that learning French involves ways of using language that may be unfamiliar (e.g. using merci when refusing an offer), and some ways of behaving and thinking that may be unfamiliar (e.g. the importance of food/meals in some families and regional traditions, different ways of expressing or describing feelings or relationships, and the more formal relationship between teacher and student)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing cultural meanings in expressions such as le goûter, la rentrée and la bise by making comparisons to their own context, for example, What do they consider to be le goûter compared to French children?

as_extracts.name: LFREF102-E14
as_extracts.description: They recognise that French is spoken in communities and regions in Australia and around the world, and relate this to their own language(s) and culture(s).

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2U06 - French
content_descriptions.text: identify where French is used around the world and recognise that there are many different languages spoken in communities throughout Australia
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching the countries where different languages are spoken and discussing why the world has many different languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching symbols and colours used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and by French-speaking communities in a range of contexts, for example, identifying the colours on a range of flags from different countries and communities in French, and discussing what the colours represent in English

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that many languages from different parts of the world are spoken in Australia and may be represented in their classroom, and creating a speech bubble that introduces them and the language(s) they speak

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages and communities have different protocols regarding the use of terms of respect, for example, there are ways of addressing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples using familial terms (e.g. ‘Uncle’ or ‘Aunty’) depending on the relationship, and comparing these terms with those in French and/or other languages

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the names of French landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as Mont Blanc

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that French is spoken in many different places in the world apart from mainland France, and using a globe or a printed/digital world map to highlight francophone countries or places (and imagining why French is spoken there)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing examples of how gestures and body language are similar to or different in French to the language(s) they speak at home

curriculum_content_description.strand_title: Engaging with French Language and Culture
curriculum_content_description.strand_tag: Engaging with French Language and Culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2E01 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: notice that French looks and sounds different to other languages
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with French Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing the word for ‘hello’ in languages known to them

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reproducing the sounds and rhythms of French by repeating after and imitating the teacher, through choral repetition or chants

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using French versions of spontaneous exclamations or interactions, such as Aïe ! or Ouf !, and the gestures that accompany them

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the different languages spoken by members of the class, and listening to the different sounds and ways of saying common expressions such as ‘Good morning’ or ‘My name is …’

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with sounds that are unique to French, such as un in brun or in in matin, imitating the shape of the teacher’s mouth and the sounds they produce

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that French uses the Roman alphabet like English but that, unlike English, some French letters use diacritic marks to indicate a change in pronunciation, and then racing each other to point to the letters with a diacritic mark

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the use of diacritic marks can change the sound of letters, for example, noticing that a cedilla on a c (ç) makes it sound like an s, and noticing the use of acute and grave accent marks

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E01-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing songs, rhymes and action stories, using non-verbal forms of expression such as gestures, facial expressions and body language to support understanding

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2E02 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: develop oral language skills through exploring and listening to the sounds and patterns of the language
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with French Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using call-and-response chants and songs to develop question-and-answer responses, for example, the teacher chanting, Est-ce que tout le monde est prêt ?, and the students responding, Oui, Madame/Monsieur, on est prêt !

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with new sets of vocabulary by making concrete associations with them, such as touching and identifying colours in the classroom, or touching and identifying soft-toy animals and naming them

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: associating actions with common verbs, nouns and adjectives to facilitate vocabulary recall, such as making an eating gesture for Je mange or a happy face for Je suis content

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing likes and dislikes such as colours, animals, food, sport and hobbies, possibly using images, props or digital prompts

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the intonation patterns and understanding the difference between statements, questions and exclamations, for example, Tu as 6 ans. / Tu as 6 ans ! / Tu as 6 ans ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: transforming simple statements into questions by raising their voice at the end, for example, Tu manges une banane. / Tu manges une banane ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing hand gestures, intonation patterns and facial expressions that accompany some expressions of French, for example, noticing shrugs or exclamations (e.g. Bof !; Mais non !; Oh là là !), and practising these expressions and body language with a partner; or responding with the appropriate French expression to the teacher role-playing different scenarios (e.g. the teacher asking whether they attend school during the night, and the students responding, Mais non !)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing simple games such as ‘go fish’, using colours or numbers, basic question forms, and affirmative and negative responses, for example, Tu as un sept ? Oui, voilà !; Et toi, tu as le jaune ? Non, j’ai le vert

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: facilitating turn-taking and sharing in play by using French expressions, for example, integrating expressions into aspects of their play with friends, such as À mon/ton tour; C’est à moi/toi; Vas-y !; D’accord; C’est parti !

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E02-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: integrating French words and expressions spontaneously into their play in the classroom, as well as at recess or other occasions, for example, Voilà; Pardon; Merci; Je suis désolé; Ah bon; S’il te plaît

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2E03 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and respond to greetings, instructions and language relating to their personal world using one- or 2-word responses and/or single-idea phrases
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with French Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E03-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing themselves and responding to greetings, for example, Comment t’appelles-tu ? Je m’appelle …; Ça va, Céline ? Ça va (bien), merci

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E03-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: forming a circle and creating a question-and-answer routine, asking the student next to them and so forth, for example, Je m’appelle Céline. Et toi, comment t’appelles-tu ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E03-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using French songs or rhymes for everyday routines (e.g. roll call, opening and closing lessons), for example, reciting ‘Bonjour, mes amis. / Au revoir, mes amis.’ or ‘Rangeons la salle de classe’

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E03-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to instructions or directions through actions, gestures or verbal responses (e.g. On fait un grand cercle; Lève-toi; Regardez-moi), or call-and-response routines (e.g. Un, deux, trois, arrête. Tout le monde met ses mains sur sa tête.)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E03-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to games or songs with actions, for example, ‘Tête, épaules, genoux et pieds’

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E03-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to basic classroom instructions using simple imperative verb forms, for example, Viens ici !; Écoutez bien !; Écrivez votre nom.; Fermez la porte !

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E03-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using French phrases for everyday interactions (e.g. Bon appétit !), thanking and apologising (e.g. Merci !; Oh pardon !; De rien !; Excusez-moi.), or special occasions such as birthdays and other celebrations (e.g. Bonne fête !; Bravo !)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2E04 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: explore connections between language and culture through play and/or imagination
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with French Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures, facial expressions and body language through games such as charades, or by incorporating them into stories, plays or songs to enhance meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing simple French games that are similar to Australian ones (e.g. à la déli-delo, le fermier dans son pré), and/or playing traditional outdoor French children’s games (e.g. 1, 2, 3 soleil; cache-cache; la marelle; le jeu de l’escargot)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing and engaging with cultural items from French-speaking countries, such as Euros, postcards and authentic items

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging ideas, feelings and understandings of language and culture through play-based experiences such as dress-ups, puppets, and pretend cafés and French shops such as la boulangerie and le marché

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that different kinds of language (including spoken and body language) are used in different situations with different people, for example, observing exchanges between children and parents (e.g. Un bisou, Papa ! Je t’aime chéri(e).) and exchanges with unfamiliar adults (e.g. Bonjour Madame, comment allez-vous ?)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing gestures to convey different messages, such as indicating that they think someone is not telling the truth by pointing to their own eye and saying Mon oeil !, for example, playing the game ‘2 truths and a lie’, using a simple structure such as name, age and favourite colour

elaborations.name: VC2LF2E04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected to culture, such as eating pancakes on Mardi Gras or making la bûche de Noël for Christmas

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2C01 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: communicate using formulaic and modelled language relating to aspects of their personal world

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to Comment ça va ? with a variety of expressions such as Ça va bien., Ça va mal. and Je suis content(e)/triste. as they enter the classroom or during a ‘one-minute challenge’ classroom activity (e.g. greeting as many people in French as they can in one minute)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of the class, introducing themselves and responding to everyday personal questions such as Quel âge as-tu ?, Où habites-tu ? and As-tu un animal domestique ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: naming family members and friends and noticing the difference between the formal and informal forms, such as mère/maman and grandmère/mamie

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and sharing simple expressions and songs with friends and family, for example, singing ‘Joyeux anniversaire’ and using appropriate greetings (e.g. Salut !; Bonsoir !; Felicitations !) for different times or occasions

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using puppets or printouts from popular shows or cartoons to role-play greetings and exchange information, imagining themselves as the character

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic expressions to ask questions related to their needs, for example, Est-ce que je peux aller aux toilettes ?; Est-ce que je peux boire de l’eau ?; Est-ce que je peux avoir une gomme ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to simple questions on topics such as home, school or pets, using supporting intonation and gestures, for example, C’est qui ? C’est Maman.; Qu’est-ce que c’est ? C’est une chaise.; Où est …? Il est …; C’est un chien ? Non, c’est un chat !

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C01-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using PowerPoint slides or image flashcards to show different pictures (using taught vocabulary) to elicit responses

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C01-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple descriptive or expressive statements to describe themselves and to express their likes, preferences or feelings (e.g. Moi, j’ai cinq ans; Je suis australien; J’aime le sport; Je préfère la danse; Je suis très content), for example, creating a flipbook (on paper or digitally), drawing/pasting in images to support their sentences

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2C02 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in a range of guided language activities using formulaic expressions, and visual and spoken cues

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: generating phrases (e.g. Je suis triste; Je suis malade) using props such as images of faces with different expressions, for example, randomly distributing emoji faces attached to an icy pole stick and asking each student, Comment ça va ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary, for example, practising high-frequency verbs using flashcards with images and/or written words, and using gestures to accompany the verbs where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing simple memory games (e.g. Je vais au marché et je vais acheter … to practise vocabulary for fruit and vegetable names), or playing cards to match words or phrases with images

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: repeating simple sentence patterns such as subject+verb+object and interchanging the words, for example, Elle/Il mange une banane; Je lance/mange une pomme; Je mange une pomme / un sandwich

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a pocket chart with individual words and accompanying images to scaffold sentence building, for example, Je | mange | un ananas / une pomme / une fraise

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a scaffold to interchange sentence content (e.g. Je vais au café/restaurant/musée), and using accompanying images to make concrete connections

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C02-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a template to create a longer text, for example, playing a guessing game to guess the name of an animal by asking for clues (e.g. Je suis grand/gris; J’habite dans l’océan; Je mange des poissons)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C02-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using some prepositions in simple sentence structures, for example, using mini-whiteboards to draw prepositional sentences uttered by the teacher (e.g. Le chat est sous la table)

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2C03 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate key information in a variety of texts with support, and respond using gestures, images, words and/or formulaic phrases
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing an image and identifying the main idea or event based on images (e.g. l’anniversaire, le zoo, la maison), talking about their understanding with a partner, and then sharing with the class

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words in a variety of texts by matching images with words, for example, reading texts with pictograms to facilitate understanding of difficult or previously unseen words

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising words and phrases in French texts that look, sound and have the same meaning in English, for example, examining a word collage of places in a town and identifying the similarities, such as banque/bank and poste / post office

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and assigning symbols, titles, words and labels to classroom items and resources or personal possessions, such as la table, le livre, l’ordinateur and la carte

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: highlighting keywords and points in a variety of texts, such as stories (e.g. ‘Les Trois Petits Cochons’; Le Petit Chaperon rouge’; ‘Les Amis de la ferme’), rhymes and songs, and adding them to a word wall in their classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images in catalogues, naming toys and games such as jouets pour les tout-petits, and selecting and listing items and prices

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing video clips with subtitles in either French or English to make connections to meaning and/or pronunciation; or viewing a silent animated film or a video with no sound, and then imagining what the characters are saying and/or describing the action or scene

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a story such as ‘La Chenille qui fait des trous' and watching the video, pausing to reiterate known words and/or make observations, and miming, drawing, pointing, clicking or dragging to show their understanding of key points

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to texts by sequencing pictures and simple text in the order that events occurred, or by creating a storyboard to retell a story or information

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C03-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a ‘Big Book’ or viewing a PowerPoint of a known text such as ‘Les Trois Petits Cochons’, and making informed guesses for words that have been covered up or blanked out

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2C04 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: explore and make meaning from sounds, words and phrases for familiar objects or terms in French through play, and discover how languages influence each other
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising simple number concepts such as quatre, using charts and counters

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: grouping vocabulary (e.g. classroom objects, animals) into sets by using word cards and/or images, and playing games (e.g. ‘buzz’, ‘around the world’) to practise numbers or other vocabulary sets

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using and manipulating classroom aids such as coloured shapes to create understanding of number, adjectives and word order, for example, J’ai trois cercles rouges et deux rectangles bleus

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and comparing familiar onomatopoeia in French and English, such as ouaf ouaf (woof woof) and groin groin (oink oink), and then making the relevant noise when their teacher says the name of the animal, or listening to recordings of animals and saying their names in French

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages have loan words and that many French words are used in English (e.g. croissant, restaurant, menu, ballet) by creating a categories chart to list words from different languages, or playing a sorting game to sort words into their language of origin

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that many English words are used in French (e.g. le weekend, le parking, le cowboy)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing physical or digital board games (e.g. 4 in a row, concentration, snakes and ladders, bingo) that have been modified to help students learn vocabulary or practise question-and-answer exchanges

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cognates to make informed guesses about the meaning of French words such as l’hôpital (hospital) and un tigre (tiger), for example, reading a story about a family who can’t decide what pet to buy at a pet store and identifying words such as une tortue and un lézard

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing ‘hide-and-seek’ with classroom objects, for example, Où est le crayon ? Sous la table. / Dans la trousse.

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C04-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing role-plays, such as buying fruits and vegetables, or acting as a character from a story that is familiar to the class

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2C05 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using words, familiar phrases and modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: to form letters of simple words such as rouge, or tracing letters to write simple words or phrases, for example, tracing J’ai cinq ans, and putting 5 candles on the image of a cake

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling images with words or short phrases, such as Il y a trois crayons

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing information about themselves using modelled language (e.g. J’ai … ans; J’aime la couleur …; J’habite à …; Mon anniversaire, c’est le …), and recording role-plays of greetings or other everyday interactions

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a mini-autobiography or a family album using simple text and photographs, pictures or drawings, for example, writing Voici ma mère, and drawing a picture to match

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital glossary of new French words and phrases with accompanying drawings, pictures or photos, for example, creating a collage or booklet of fruits and labelling them

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing poems, rhymes or simple stories (e.g. ‘Le Navet géant’; ‘Boucles d’or et les trois ours’) that include repeated phrases and rhythms to emphasise key points, for example, chanting Au loup !

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple evaluative statements about their favourite characters in stories, rhymes or songs, for example, Il est magnifique !; J’adore Minou !; Elle est sympa !

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating stories, rhymes and songs with drawings or digital tools, using simple or complex sentences and captions, or using puppets, gestures and props to retell stories

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple questions to interview a member of the class and then creating a student profile about them with simple sentences, for example, Tu t’appelles comment ?; Tu as un animal chez toi ?; Tu aimes les fraises ?; Tu es grand ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF2C05-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a survey or tally about members of the class (e.g. what fruits they like/dislike or their birthday month) and then creating a display wall with pictures and captions

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2U01 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: imitate the pronunciation and intonation of spoken French, and understand how sounds are produced

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reciting the French alphabet and/or singing alphabet rhymes/songs, and noticing that the French and English alphabets are both based on the Roman alphabet, but that the letters have different names in French and represent different sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the facial movements involved with making sound blends in French, especially with vowel sounds (e.g. eu in fleur)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: saying and comparing the feeling of different vocal movements when practising sounds such as ou and eu

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing letters at the end of certain French words that are silent (e.g. chat/chats, riz, deux, cahier), for example, playing a ‘wrong word’ pronunciation game, where they circle the mispronounced words in a wordlist, focusing on the endings

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that diacritic marks can change the pronunciation of letters in words such as français (cedilla) and marché (acute accent)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: building phonic awareness by experimenting with sounds, focusing on those that are initially difficult (e.g. u in tu, r in très rapide and ion in Attention !) and listening closely to distinguish between sounds such as bon/bien/beau or chien/chat/champ

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that spoken French uses liaisons and that each word within a phrase may not necessarily be heard as a discrete, individual word, for example, vous‿allez; deux‿amis; trois‿heures

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2U02 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify sound combinations to produce simple words, and then an increasing number of frequently used words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising basic sound combinations in French and how these may differ from English, such as ch in chat, qu in quel(le) and in in matin, by using snappy chants such as ‘Never chat with your chat!’ or ‘Don’t be so quick to say “kwuh” in quel!’

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the nasal sounds in French, such as on in mon and an in dans

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the differences between how phonograms are pronounced in English and French (e.g. oi in English ‘coin’ vs. French trois)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the sounds of more complex combinations such as ille in famille or eau in cadeau

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common adjectives for colour and size in various contexts, such as classroom items (e.g. une petite trousse rouge) and animals (e.g. un grand cheval brun)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using high-frequency verbs in a variety of contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U02-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: underlining rhyming words or graphemes in short texts or poems

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2U03 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and explore how the Roman alphabet and features of language are used to construct meaning in French

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U03-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: becoming familiar with the French alphabet, noticing similarities to and differences from English, for example, double-v (pronounced ‘dooble-vé’) and i-grec (pronounced ‘ee-grec’), by singing the alphabet, and discussing similarities and differences in the sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U03-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing the possible confusion between how the letters g and j are pronounced in English and French, providing examples such as girafe, gentil, joli and jaune, and practising the correct pronunciation when playing ‘snap’ with words or images featuring these sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U03-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how the letter h in French is always silent (e.g. ‘hibou never says “whoo”’), and practising the pronunciation of words such as hôpital, hôtel and hockey

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2U04 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify that written and spoken French has grammatical structures and other language features that may be similar to or different from English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that French and English use punctuation conventions such as full stops, capital letters, commas and question marks

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the similarities between the English and French subject+verb+object structure (e.g. Je mange la pomme; Tu as le cahier), using vocabulary cards to arrange sentences following this structure, reading similar sentences and noticing that adjectives are used to describe people, animals, objects or places and are usually placed after the noun, and brainstorming a rule for using adjectives in sentences, for example, colour goes after a noun (e.g. le chien noir; le papillon rose)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: becoming aware of grammatical gender, noticing and using masculine or feminine forms of nouns and adjectives such as le chien, la maison, le copain, la copine, le petit garçon and la petite fille

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing number knowledge, and identifying the similarities and differences between the use of cardinal and ordinal numbers in English and French, for example, using ordinals for days of the month in English but only for the first day of each month in French (e.g. le premier mars; le 2 juin)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: becoming aware of adjective agreement with masculine and feminine (and then plural) nouns, and noticing that the feminine adjective necessitates a change (e.g. une pomme verte), for example, using a pocket chart with colour-coded articles and nouns (to indicate gender), and ‘matching’ them with the appropriate masculine or feminine adjectives

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2U05 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on how language, culture and identity are interconnected and discuss how French-speaking communities are similar to or different from others
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing their own use of words, expressions or behaviours that make them who they are, including words from different languages known to the class and ways of celebrating or talking that may not be familiar to other people

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a short video and noticing formalities in French-speaking communities such as handshakes, la bise or standing up to greet a visitor to the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading a French children’s book about school and family life, and comparing aspects of Australian and French children’s lifestyles, such as school canteen meals or daily greetings between family members or friends

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that learning French involves ways of using language that may be unfamiliar (e.g. using merci when refusing an offer), and some ways of behaving and thinking that may be unfamiliar (e.g. the importance of food/meals in some families and regional traditions, different ways of expressing or describing feelings or relationships, and the more formal relationship between teacher and student)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U05-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing cultural meanings in expressions such as le goûter, la rentrée and la bise by making comparisons to their own context, for example, What do they consider to be le goûter compared to French children?

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LF2U06 - French
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify where French is used around the world and recognise that there are many different languages spoken in communities throughout Australia
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching the countries where different languages are spoken and discussing why the world has many different languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching symbols and colours used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and by French-speaking communities in a range of contexts, for example, identifying the colours on a range of flags from different countries and communities in French, and discussing what the colours represent in English

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that many languages from different parts of the world are spoken in Australia and may be represented in their classroom, and creating a speech bubble that introduces them and the language(s) they speak

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages and communities have different protocols regarding the use of terms of respect, for example, there are ways of addressing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples using familial terms (e.g. ‘Uncle’ or ‘Aunty’) depending on the relationship, and comparing these terms with those in French and/or other languages

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the names of French landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as Mont Blanc

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that French is spoken in many different places in the world apart from mainland France, and using a globe or a printed/digital world map to highlight francophone countries or places (and imagining why French is spoken there)

elaborations.name: VC2LF2U06-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing examples of how gestures and body language are similar to or different in French to the language(s) they speak at home

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 3 and 4, French language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. Students communicate and work in collaboration with their peers and teachers through purposeful and creative play in structured activities that involve listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing. They use French to interact with their peers and teachers and to participate in activities in familiar settings that reflect their interests and capabilities. They use local and digital resources to explore French-speaking communities. They continue to receive extensive support through modelling, scaffolding and repetition, as well as the use of targeted resources.

Students develop active listening skills and use gestures, words and modelled expressions, imitating the sounds, pronunciation and intonation of French. They locate information, and respond to and create texts using written and spoken French. They access authentic and purpose-developed French-language texts such as picture books, stories, songs, digital and animated games, timetables, recipes and advertisements. They recognise the interconnected nature of language, culture and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 4, students use French to initiate structured interactions and share information related to the classroom and their personal worlds. They use modelled language to participate in spoken and written activities. They locate and respond to key items of information in texts, using strategies to help interpret and convey meaning in familiar contexts. They use modelled language and basic grammatical structures to create texts.

Students imitate the sound combinations and rhythms of spoken French. They demonstrate their understanding that French has non-verbal, spoken and written language conventions and rules to convey meaning. They recognise that some terms have cultural meanings. They identify patterns in French and make comparisons between French and English, using simple metalanguage. They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

as_extracts.name: LFREF104-E01
as_extracts.description: students use French to initiate structured interactions and share information related to the classroom and their personal worlds.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4C01 - French
content_descriptions.text: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about themselves, others and the classroom environment, using formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating and exchanging greetings, offering wishes for particular occasions, situations or times of day in formal and informal contexts (e.g. Bonjour, Madame Patou. Comment allez-vous ?; Salut Nicole, ça va ? Pas mal, et toi ?; Bonne nuit, Papa !; Bonne fête !; À demain, Mademoiselle; À bientôt !; Joyeux anniversaire !; Bon courage !), for example, viewing images of a birthday party, and deciding which expression would be appropriate for the situation or role-playing an interaction in that scenario

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common responses to frequently asked questions or comments, imitating modelled intonation and stress patterns (e.g. Très bien; Voilà; Oui, bien sûr; D’accord; Hein; Bah … oui !)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to instructions, or asking for help or clarification, for example, Encore une fois; Montre-moi; Chantez plus fort; Regarde les photos; Écoutez/Écrivez/Tapez la phrase; Pardon/Excusez-moi Madame/Monsieur, je ne comprends pas; Répétez, s’il vous plaît; J’ai une question; J’ai besoin d’aide

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising responses to everyday questions, for example, selecting random questions written on icy pole sticks or generated by a digital program (e.g. Où habites-tu ?; Quel âge as-tu ?; As-tu un animal chez toi ?), and replying to them using a variety of answers

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a ‘Find someone who …’ activity, expressing likes and dislikes as members of the class ask a question, for example, J’aime le chocolat, mais je déteste le fromage; Il aime la classe de musique, mais il n’aime pas le cours de sciences

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging simple correspondence with peers, such as notes, invitations or birthday cards in print or digital form

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using print or digital photographs, short videos or recordings to exchange and respond to information about themselves and their family, friends or interests, for example, J’ai deux sœurs et j’ai un frère; Je suis fils/fille unique; J’aime le sport, mais j’adore la musique !; Et toi, parle-moi de ta famille …

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cohesive devices (e.g. the conjunctions et, mais and ou) or interjections as fillers (e.g. ah bon; voilà; eh bien; alors) to enhance interactions when completing a role-play using modelled language

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4C02 - French
content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve expressing interests and exchanging information, using a range of familiar phrases and modelled structures

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing a ‘broken sentences’ activity, asking and answering questions relating to concepts such as time, place or number, including days of the week, months, dates and seasons, based on the information on their worksheet, and asking questions to fill any gaps, for example, Ça fait combien ? Ça fait cinq.; Quelle heure est-il ? Il est dix heures.; Aujourd’hui c’est vendredi ? Non, c’est jeudi.; Quel temps fait-il aujourd’hui ? C’est l’hiver. Il fait très froid.

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to est-ce que questions and recognising the difference between oui/non questions and ou questions, for example, knowing to use oui or non in response to Est-ce que le ciel est bleu ?, and knowing to select between 2 choices in Est-ce qu’un chef travaille dans un restaurant ou dans un garage ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing the French currency (Euros) to buy items (e.g. magazines, fruit, vegetables) at an imagined market or shop, for example, Ça coûte combien ? C’est cinq euros.; Le vélo noir / La bicyclette noire, c’est combien ?; 1 kilo en plus, s’il vous plaît.; Vingt grammes de moins

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing games that involve active listening, memory, information exchange and negotiating turns, for example, pige dans le lac (with vocabulary or image cards) or le jeu de sept familles, using language such as C’est à toi ? Oui, c’est à moi.; C’est ton/mon tour

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: praising each other (e.g. Pas mal !; Bon travail !; Super !; Excellent !; Bravo !) when working collaboratively with the class on tasks that require following instructions such as cooking or other step-based activities such as crafts or drawing tasks

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing a poster for a specific event or creating a picture book or word wall, and collaboratively sharing decisions about content, vocabulary and design, for example, Ceci ou cela ?; Qu’est-ce que tu préfères ?; Là ou là ?; Petit ou grand ?

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4C04 - French
content_descriptions.text: develop strategies to comprehend and produce French, adjusting language to convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning to use a dictionary to find and understand unknown words in texts

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: building their vocabulary for describing actions or feelings by accessing multimodal resources and presenting information of interest, such as les fêtes d’anniversaire, les vacances and les copains

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: strengthening vocabulary knowledge by making connections with known words such as le marché, le supermarché and le marchand

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to factual and imaginative picture and digital books, short scripted plays or animations that use familiar French words by creating a class display of the key information, and providing a glossary of new words and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting and using French words and expressions that do not translate easily into English, for example, Bon appétit !; Bon voyage !; Voilà !; Chic !

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with a familiar story, writing or acting out a plausible different ending, and using new words, expressions and gestures to convey the key messages of the story

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising inviting a partner to do something and refusing each other’s invitation politely, using formulaic and modelled expressions, for example, Je voudrais bien, mais …; Désolé(e); Malheureusement

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4C05 - French
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating personal profiles using simple words and expressions selected from word banks and modelled statements, highlighting key characteristics and features, for example, Je suis australien et grec. Je suis sportif. J’ai les yeux bleus. Je suis grand. Je suis courageux. Je parle anglais et grec. J’ai beaucoup de cousins.

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and performing alternative versions of stories or action songs, using voice, rhythm and gestures to animate characters, or using support materials such as drawings or story maps to create visual context

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a class profile, chart or database about likes, dislikes and interests (e.g. les sports préférés, les plats de choix), using multimodal resources, checklists, surveys or question cues (e.g. Tu préfères le brie ou le camembert ?; Combien de …?; À quelle heure …?)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating digital infographics or presentations to provide a combination of written and spoken information, for example, describing different jobs and including information about the workplace and tasks (e.g. Voici un médecin. Il travaille dans un hôpital. Il soigne les gens malades.)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the scene of a classroom or home using prepositional sentences, for example, La trousse verte est à côté du crayon jaune sur la table

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a map of France or a French-speaking country or region and props to record and present la météo, for example, À Paris, il fait chaud. À Nouméa, il pleut. Prends un parapluie aujourd’hui

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving a visual presentation with captions about their daily routine using formulaic reflexive verbs (e.g. Le lundi, je me lève à sept heures)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a simple instructional or procedural text, such as designing treasure hunts (e.g. Où se cache le trésor ?), or creating a recipe such as les crêpes by making a list of the ingredients and quantities (e.g. 200 grammes de farine, un verre de lait) and using imperative verb forms (e.g. ajoutez, mélangez, versez, servez)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating short imaginative texts designed to amuse or entertain, for example, stories featuring imaginary creatures with names created out of 2 or more real animal names such as le chevaloon, le lapinat or les moutaches

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using different text types (e.g. postcards, emails), styles of writing (e.g. informative, persuasive, imaginative) and the specific language conventions associated with them

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4U02 - French
content_descriptions.text: recognise and use modelled language, formulaic phrases, simple grammatical structures and language conventions to convey meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an increasing range of adjectives (e.g. bizarre, magnifique, formidable) and additional gender forms and agreements (e.g. blanc/blanche; gros/grosse; le chat blanc; la souris blanche), for example, creating a superhero avatar and describing their qualities and/or their outfit

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising word patterns and building word clusters (e.g. number knowledge from 60 to 100; ordinal numbers)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the differences between definite and indefinite articles, and how to refer to a specific or non-specific person, animal, place or object (e.g. Tu manges la pomme; le climat français; J’achète un livre; une vache énorme), for example, writing sentences that contrast and illustrate both the definite and indefinite articles (e.g. Il y a une gomme blanche sur un pupitre noir / La gomme blanche est sur le pupitre noir)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and beginning to use common verb conjugations such as regular -er verbs, for example, using the correct conjugation in cloze exercises such as Elle chante (sings), or by matching pronoun to verb in digital apps and using the click-and-drag option to move the conjugated verb to the correct pronoun

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing negation in simple sentence structures and colloquial expressions (e.g. Je ne sais pas; Elle ne mange pas; Tu ne viens pas ?; Pas du tout !), understanding that the ne and pas ‘sandwich’ the verb, and practising this negative formation by transforming positive sentences into negative sentences, for example, transforming Je lave la voiture to Je ne lave pas la voiture on mini-whiteboards

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions to indicate direction or location (e.g. à gauche, à droite, à côté de), for example, giving instructions to a partner to draw furniture on a bedroom template (e.g. Il y a une lampe sur la commode)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing the relationship between subject pronouns (e.g. je/tu/il/elle) and the present tense endings of verbs associated with familiar actions and environments, for example, Il chante bien; Je suis fatigué; Tu aimes le yaourt; Elle est en classe

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled common irregular verbs (e.g. être, avoir, aller, faire), for example, Je suis intelligent(e); Tu as quel âge ?; Comment allez-vous ?; Il va à la plage; Je fais le petit-déjeuner, and choosing between them in cloze exercises such as Il ____ un gâteau. (est, fait, va)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing an awareness of verb tenses and reflexive verbs with modelled support, for example, J’ai fini !; Je me lève; Je me brosse les dents

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U02-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some adverbs to elaborate on simple statements, for example, Elle mange lentement; Je chante doucement; Il parle très vite

as_extracts.name: LFREF104-E03
as_extracts.description: They locate and respond to key items of information in texts, using strategies to help interpret and convey meaning in familiar contexts.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4C03 - French
content_descriptions.text: locate and respond to key information related to familiar content obtained from spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading simple narratives, responding to images that evoke positive or negative emotions (e.g. affection, sadness, anger), and making connections with their own experiences by using stem statements, for example, Je suis fou/folle quand …; Je suis content(e) si …; J’ai peur de …

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a text that presents 2 distinct points of view on a familiar topic, listening for key arguments and generating a PMI chart or other similar mind map

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing simple notes, invitations and birthday cards, giving these to another student in the class, and then responding to their correspondence in print or digital form

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing thought-provoking images and responding to prompts, for example, Je vois …; Je pense …; J’imagine …

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting and using favourite exclamations, words or expressions from texts (e.g. Terrible !; Ça y est !; Pas vrai !; Quoi de neuf ?), and incorporating them into speech or thought bubbles in a comic strip

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to short spoken texts with some unfamiliar language and identifying points of information, for example, the name and phone number left in a voicemail, the age of a child being interviewed, items on a shopping list, or information in a weather report from a French-speaking location

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting information from print or digital sources about topics of interest, such as les animaux domestiques/sauvages, and creating a display with names and appropriate adjectives

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a story, song, cartoon, comic or simple narrative by retelling or re-enacting the main events, taking on the role of a character or matching pictures with descriptive statements

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing short videos and extrapolating details, for example, watching the daily routine of a student and inferring the time (e.g. À sept heures et quart, elle mange son petit déjeuner)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C03-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating information about activities in a French school (e.g. l’emploi du temps; la lecture; l’orthographe; le vocabulaire; les mathématiques), comparing this with their own daily schedule, and noting any differences and similarities

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4C04 - French
content_descriptions.text: develop strategies to comprehend and produce French, adjusting language to convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning to use a dictionary to find and understand unknown words in texts

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: building their vocabulary for describing actions or feelings by accessing multimodal resources and presenting information of interest, such as les fêtes d’anniversaire, les vacances and les copains

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: strengthening vocabulary knowledge by making connections with known words such as le marché, le supermarché and le marchand

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to factual and imaginative picture and digital books, short scripted plays or animations that use familiar French words by creating a class display of the key information, and providing a glossary of new words and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting and using French words and expressions that do not translate easily into English, for example, Bon appétit !; Bon voyage !; Voilà !; Chic !

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with a familiar story, writing or acting out a plausible different ending, and using new words, expressions and gestures to convey the key messages of the story

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising inviting a partner to do something and refusing each other’s invitation politely, using formulaic and modelled expressions, for example, Je voudrais bien, mais …; Désolé(e); Malheureusement

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4U03 - French
content_descriptions.text: recognise and compare familiar French language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using simple metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U03-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering French words used in English (e.g. restaurant, café, chauffeur, ballet, croissant) and English words used by French speakers (e.g. le coach, le blog, l’internet, le football, le burger, le sandwich, le denim), comparing how they are pronounced differently by looking at a collection of English words used in French, and then competing with a partner to be the first person to point out the word the teacher says

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U03-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that French has close connections to other languages that have shared histories and many similar words, for example, ‘bank’ (English), la banque (French), la banca (Italian) and el banco (Spanish); ‘art’ (English), l’art (French), l’arte (Italian) and el arte (Spanish)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U03-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and comparing keywords in French and English versions of favourite stories such as ‘La Chenille qui fait des trous' or ‘La Vieille Dame qui avala une mouche’, and considering the rhythms and vocal effects in each version

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U03-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing and applying features of familiar types of texts (e.g. weather reports, postcards, recipes); recognising how different textual elements combine to make meaning (e.g. the images, font and script of a webpage; the layout, title and illustrations in a picture book; the highlighting of names, dates and times in an invitation); and creating visual displays to exhibit in the classroom, which present the text types taken from real examples in French magazines, websites, children’s books or newspapers

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U03-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising features of a simple spoken or written text in French (e.g. a verbal greeting or a written message), for example, noting terms of address and ways of signing off, and comparing them with similar texts in English

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U03-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating examples of shortened noun forms in colloquial French (e.g. le resto, le frigo, le foot, le prof) from websites, guessing their meaning and comparing them with abbreviations in Australian English (e.g. brekkie, arvo)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4U03-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing parts of a sentence using metalanguage (e.g. noun, verb, adverb, adjective) to describe words, and noticing the word order and patterns, for example, the suffix -ment is usually used in adverbs and those adverbs usually follow the verb, which is similar to -ly adverbs in English

as_extracts.name: LFREF104-E04
as_extracts.description: They use modelled language and basic grammatical structures to create texts.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4C01 - French
content_descriptions.text: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about themselves, others and the classroom environment, using formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating and exchanging greetings, offering wishes for particular occasions, situations or times of day in formal and informal contexts (e.g. Bonjour, Madame Patou. Comment allez-vous ?; Salut Nicole, ça va ? Pas mal, et toi ?; Bonne nuit, Papa !; Bonne fête !; À demain, Mademoiselle; À bientôt !; Joyeux anniversaire !; Bon courage !), for example, viewing images of a birthday party, and deciding which expression would be appropriate for the situation or role-playing an interaction in that scenario

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common responses to frequently asked questions or comments, imitating modelled intonation and stress patterns (e.g. Très bien; Voilà; Oui, bien sûr; D’accord; Hein; Bah … oui !)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to instructions, or asking for help or clarification, for example, Encore une fois; Montre-moi; Chantez plus fort; Regarde les photos; Écoutez/Écrivez/Tapez la phrase; Pardon/Excusez-moi Madame/Monsieur, je ne comprends pas; Répétez, s’il vous plaît; J’ai une question; J’ai besoin d’aide

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising responses to everyday questions, for example, selecting random questions written on icy pole sticks or generated by a digital program (e.g. Où habites-tu ?; Quel âge as-tu ?; As-tu un animal chez toi ?), and replying to them using a variety of answers

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a ‘Find someone who …’ activity, expressing likes and dislikes as members of the class ask a question, for example, J’aime le chocolat, mais je déteste le fromage; Il aime la classe de musique, mais il n’aime pas le cours de sciences

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging simple correspondence with peers, such as notes, invitations or birthday cards in print or digital form

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using print or digital photographs, short videos or recordings to exchange and respond to information about themselves and their family, friends or interests, for example, J’ai deux sœurs et j’ai un frère; Je suis fils/fille unique; J’aime le sport, mais j’adore la musique !; Et toi, parle-moi de ta famille …

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C01-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cohesive devices (e.g. the conjunctions et, mais and ou) or interjections as fillers (e.g. ah bon; voilà; eh bien; alors) to enhance interactions when completing a role-play using modelled language

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4C02 - French
content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve expressing interests and exchanging information, using a range of familiar phrases and modelled structures

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing a ‘broken sentences’ activity, asking and answering questions relating to concepts such as time, place or number, including days of the week, months, dates and seasons, based on the information on their worksheet, and asking questions to fill any gaps, for example, Ça fait combien ? Ça fait cinq.; Quelle heure est-il ? Il est dix heures.; Aujourd’hui c’est vendredi ? Non, c’est jeudi.; Quel temps fait-il aujourd’hui ? C’est l’hiver. Il fait très froid.

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to est-ce que questions and recognising the difference between oui/non questions and ou questions, for example, knowing to use oui or non in response to Est-ce que le ciel est bleu ?, and knowing to select between 2 choices in Est-ce qu’un chef travaille dans un restaurant ou dans un garage ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing the French currency (Euros) to buy items (e.g. magazines, fruit, vegetables) at an imagined market or shop, for example, Ça coûte combien ? C’est cinq euros.; Le vélo noir / La bicyclette noire, c’est combien ?; 1 kilo en plus, s’il vous plaît.; Vingt grammes de moins

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing games that involve active listening, memory, information exchange and negotiating turns, for example, pige dans le lac (with vocabulary or image cards) or le jeu de sept familles, using language such as C’est à toi ? Oui, c’est à moi.; C’est ton/mon tour

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: praising each other (e.g. Pas mal !; Bon travail !; Super !; Excellent !; Bravo !) when working collaboratively with the class on tasks that require following instructions such as cooking or other step-based activities such as crafts or drawing tasks

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing a poster for a specific event or creating a picture book or word wall, and collaboratively sharing decisions about content, vocabulary and design, for example, Ceci ou cela ?; Qu’est-ce que tu préfères ?; Là ou là ?; Petit ou grand ?

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF4C05 - French
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating personal profiles using simple words and expressions selected from word banks and modelled statements, highlighting key characteristics and features, for example, Je suis australien et grec. Je suis sportif. J’ai les yeux bleus. Je suis grand. Je suis courageux. Je parle anglais et grec. J’ai beaucoup de cousins.

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and performing alternative versions of stories or action songs, using voice, rhythm and gestures to animate characters, or using support materials such as drawings or story maps to create visual context

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a class profile, chart or database about likes, dislikes and interests (e.g. les sports préférés, les plats de choix), using multimodal resources, checklists, surveys or question cues (e.g. Tu préfères le brie ou le camembert ?; Combien de …?; À quelle heure …?)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating digital infographics or presentations to provide a combination of written and spoken information, for example, describing different jobs and including information about the workplace and tasks (e.g. Voici un médecin. Il travaille dans un hôpital. Il soigne les gens malades.)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing the scene of a classroom or home using prepositional sentences, for example, La trousse verte est à côté du crayon jaune sur la table

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a map of France or a French-speaking country or region and props to record and present la météo, for example, À Paris, il fait chaud. À Nouméa, il pleut. Prends un parapluie aujourd’hui

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving a visual presentation with captions about their daily routine using formulaic reflexive verbs (e.g. Le lundi, je me lève à sept heures)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a simple instructional or procedural text, such as designing treasure hunts (e.g. Où se cache le trésor ?), or creating a recipe such as les crêpes by making a list of the ingredients and quantities (e.g. 200 grammes de farine, un verre de lait) and using imperative verb forms (e.g. ajoutez, mélangez, versez, servez)

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating short imaginative texts designed to amuse or entertain, for example, stories featuring imaginary creatures with names created out of 2 or more real animal names such as le chevaloon, le lapinat or les moutaches

elaborations.name: VC2LF4C05-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using different text types (e.g. postcards, emails), styles of writing (e.g. informative, persuasive, imaginative) and the specific language conventions associated with them

content_descriptions.text: recognise and use modelled language, formulaic phrases, simple grammatical structures and language conventions to convey meaning

elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions to indicate direction or location (e.g. à gauche, à droite, à côté de), for example, giving instructions to a partner to draw furniture on a bedroom template (e.g. Il y a une lampe sur la commode)

elaborations.elaboration_text: observing the relationship between subject pronouns (e.g. je/tu/il/elle) and the present tense endings of verbs associated with familiar actions and environments, for example, Il chante bien; Je suis fatigué; Tu aimes le yaourt; Elle est en classe

elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled common irregular verbs (e.g. être, avoir, aller, faire), for example, Je suis intelligent(e); Tu as quel âge ?; Comment allez-vous ?; Il va à la plage; Je fais le petit-déjeuner, and choosing between them in cloze exercises such as Il ____ un gâteau.
