elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing extracts from expressive contemporary texts (e.g. tales, poems, songs, dance, street art, performances), including influences from minority groups and subcultures, and identifying and comparing elements of cultural traditions in Australia and the French-speaking world

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or reading an article or interview of a well-known Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander person, discussing their opinions and ideas in French, and creating and presenting their personal profile to the class

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: obtaining information from a range of viewed texts, including photographs, maps, illustrations and weather reports; using the ‘see, think, wonder’ thinking routine to identify and extract information; summarising the main points; and presenting the key information in their own words

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: summarising the key points from a range of texts such as social media and interviews

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying underlying values and cultural references in different texts, such as an advertisement or article, and evaluating their effect on audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining graphs, a table of statistics or pictures, and using the information gained from the texts to respond orally or in written form, for example, writing a formal letter to a member of parliament, requesting change based on evidence from the texts

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C04 - French
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to respond to non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and produce texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying vocabulary and expressions associated with particular elements of French lifestyles (e.g. la cuisine, la mode, les loisirs, la famille) in film or television clips, noting how the vocabulary changes according to audience and context, for example, les recettes de grands chefs / la cuisine en cinq minutes; la famille traditionnelle/recomposée … la belle mère / le beau père

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining information obtained from different sources to compare how young people are represented in the media (e.g. comparing letters to the editor about young people with blog posts written by young people), and responding in either oral or written form; for example, creating their own letter to the editor based on the opinions they have formed after obtaining information on the topic

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing short informative texts (e.g. documentary excerpts or news reports), and responding in written or oral form, for example, creating a speech to inform people about school stress or the dangers of climate change

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: conducting surveys or structured interviews with members of the class or online French-speaking contacts, comparing their opinions and perspectives on community or personal issues, identifying social or cultural variations, and reporting the findings back to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing excerpts from interviews with public figures (e.g. politicians, sports stars, musicians, actors), noting how vocabulary, phrases or gestures are used to emphasise or clarify key information, and collating a list of new phrases and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to popular French songs or viewing French music videos, summarising key ideas or messages, and comparing these with songs and music videos that appeal to young people in Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting cultural differences, protocols and conventions in genres such as selection criteria for job applications, lettre de motivation and formules de politesse, for example, responding to a job advertisement from a French website or newspaper

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting textual conventions popular with young French speakers, such as contractions, abbreviations and acronyms used in text messaging, for example, writing and responding to a series of text messages using acronyms such as bjr = bonjour, A+ = à plus, biz = bisous, and 12C4 = un de ces quatre

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U03 - French
content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate French texts, using metalanguage to analyse language structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using metalanguage in English or French to identify the grammatical differences between languages or between their own first language and other languages they know, such as word order, verb moods and tenses, for example, the present perfect (le passé composé), possessive pronouns (les articles possessifs), agreements of adjectives and participles (l’accord des adjectifs et du participe passé), auxiliary verbs, and direct/indirect object pronouns

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing grammatical structures using metalanguage, for example, using relative clauses, relative pronouns and demonstrative adjectives to choose between qui, que and dont

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding when to use le passé composé and l’imparfait, comparing them with the equivalent terms in English

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing spoken and written texts such as apologies or invitations to identify how differences in grammar and text type determine the nature of formal and informal interactions, for example, Je t’invite ! Nous serions très heureux de vous accueillir chez nous

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how grammatical choices shade meaning and establish register, for example, the use of tu/vous to distinguish relationships; nous to suggest inclusivity or shared identity; on to suggest distance

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing sentence structures in French to English or other languages they know, and recognising the use of different clauses and tenses used to get the meaning across

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the use of personal pronouns, imperative/interrogative verb moods and emotive language in advertisements, identifying how grammatical choices, words and images combine in a text to achieve a particular purpose and effect

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U04 - French
content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the diversity of spoken forms of French from region to region (e.g. les accents du Midi; l’accent parisien, toulousain, picard) and between different French-speaking communities around the world (e.g. le Québec, La Réunion), considering how language variation can both reflect and shape social and cultural processes, with concepts such as la norme, la diversité, l’intelligibilité and les élites

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining to non-French speakers the expressions and cultural allusions encountered in French texts associated with historical, religious or civic events or traditions (e.g. la Marianne, le tricolore, la Toussaint, le 1er mai)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring intercultural communication, considering how their own cultural ways of thinking and behaving influence their own attitudes and other people’s responses or interpretations, and how attitudes can change over time

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering how the experience of learning a new language has had an impact on their awareness of their own communicative and cultural behaviours, and how these may be interpreted by others

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting gestures used by French speakers to signal meanings, such as Parfait ! and C’est fini, comparing these with gestures used in Australian English and other known languages, and using appropriate gestures when speaking French

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how language variation can reflect cultural and social identity, inclusion or exclusion, for example, reading speeches or advertisements and analysing the language used, identifying persuasive devices such as inclusive or emotive language

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the ways in which linguistic choices can vary to reflect diversity, for example, through the use of the point médian (e.g. un·e étudiant·e) and typical features of le langage épicène, such as non-gendered adjectives (e.g. aimable/sympa vs. gentil.le) and formulations (e.g. iel est une personne intéressante; iel est quelqu’un de patient)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing and discussing the interconnected nature of the linguistic and cultural diversity of French-speaking communities, and how this is also relevant to the linguistic and cultural diversity in Australia, including that of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and/or reading examples of an Acknowledgement of Country in French, and creating their own version that names the local Country for a French-speaking audience

organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

content_descriptions.text: create and present texts for diverse contexts and purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and a range of textual conventions to engage different audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information in different text types (e.g. email, article, blog post, script of a speech) for different audiences (e.g. potential consumers, voters), identifying and using relevant textual conventions to create specific types of texts, using appropriate styles of writing (e.g. imaginative, informative, persuasive, personal, evaluative)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and illustrating a children’s storybook and reading it to younger children within the school or the community, using expressive French intonation, rhythm, pitch and appropriate gestures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading an instruction manual such as mode d’emploi pour l’installation d’un logiciel, and using plain French to rephrase the instructions for a partner to follow

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a journal entry or a contribution for a school newsletter in French, reflecting on a visit to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, and, with permission, referring to cultural knowledge of the site’s significance

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or travel brochure in French for travel to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do, traditional and/or cultural considerations, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and what to wear

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a letter to the council regarding an issue about the environment, for example, informing them about an environmental concern, evaluating a service or persuading them to improve a service to help the environment

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing artwork from a local Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander artist, and then writing a script of a speech to present to a group of French speakers introducing the artist

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a role-play using language for buying and selling goods and services, for example, ordering in a bakery; selling second-hand clothes; organising travel; considering the use of planes or trains to reduce their carbon footprint; raising money for charities

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: making language choices that indicate values and attitudes when creating texts, for example, the placement of nouns and adjectives in C’est un bon à rien; C’est un brave jeune homme / C’est un jeune homme brave; Ce sont des sans-papiers / Ce sont des réfugiés

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using emotive language and images when creating texts such as reports or speeches on current issues, for example, C’est émouvant; C’est troublant; C’est déraisonnable

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U01 - French
content_descriptions.text: apply features and conventions of spoken French to extend fluency, and to respond to and create a range of texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: increasing their fluency and accuracy in spoken French by using appropriate rhythm, pitch, intonation and liaisons, and adding in the extra t if needed

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using tone and intonation to indicate emphasis or emotion, for example, Elle a fait quoi ? Il est tellement doué !

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying correct pronunciation to more complex syllable combinations, for example, la magnitude les augmentations using sentence starters and connectors to increase the complexity of their responses, for example, Normalement je me lève à six heures du matin, mais ce matin, j’ai fait la grasse matinée et je me suis levé(e) à dix heures, car c’est le weekend !

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing discussion points in an argument by using sentence starters and connectors (e.g. premièrement deuxièmement ensuite de plus en revanche)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying appropriate pauses and pace of delivery to convey meaning, emphasis, feelings and emotion, and to create effects in spoken texts, for example, recording themselves presenting a speech or participating in a conversation, and reflecting on how they could improve or adjust the delivery of the information

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: adjusting the tone of spoken or written French to reflect the formality of the context, for example, using tu and vous correctly, and conjugating the accompanying verb

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to spontaneous questions from their teachers or peers on a range of topics, for example, answering questions such as Qu’est-ce que tu as fait pendant le weekend ? Qu’est-ce que tu vas faire ce weekend ? Pourquoi tu étudies le français ? Qu’est-ce que tu aimes faire normalement ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the fluid nature of spoken language, identifying features such as interactivity and the use of repetition, pauses and interruptions; contractions such as the dropping of ne in negative structures e.g. Je sais pas trop; incomplete sentences and reliance on non-verbal elements and vocal expression such as Dis donc, t’es là ? Je suis déjà là – t’es où, toi ?

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U02 - French
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to predict meaning, and to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how grammatical choices indicate meaning, determine perspective and establish relationships, for example, how imperative verbs are used to show authority or enthusiasm, Arrêtez !; Allons-y !; Donnez-moi votre billet, Mademoiselle

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the comparative and superlative forms of adverbs and adjectives (e.g. plus vite / le plus vite; moins jolie / la moins jolie; meilleur / le meilleur), for example, reading a text and highlighting the positive, comparative and superlative adjectives in different colours, before creating a table that reflects each adjective in the different forms, and then playing a speaking game where each person adapts the sentence before by changing the adjective

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using multiple tenses (e.g. le présent, le futur proche, le futur, le passé composé, l’imparfait) and le conditionnel in both written and spoken French, for example, writing a series of short diary entries about a holiday, including details about what they did during a previous day, what their family is doing now and what they are planning to do on an upcoming day

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that verbs conjugated in the present perfect (le passé composé) with the auxiliary être (intransitive verbs, pronominal verbs and passive voice) require agreement of the past participle with the subject (e.g. Elles sont parties hier soir; Je me suis levée à sept heures; Nous nous sommes amusés; La pomme a été mangée par Pierre), as do verbs conjugated in the present perfect with the auxiliary verb avoir when preceded by the direct object pronoun (e.g. J’ai acheté des fleurs, et je les ai données à ma mère)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the imperfect (l’imparfait), and understanding how to distinguish between a completed and a continuing action in the past, for example, Nous étions déjà au lit quand il est arrivé

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the use of relative pronouns (qui, que), emphatic pronouns (e.g. moi, elle, eux), and direct and indirect object pronouns (le, la, lui, nous, vous, les, leur), and having exposure to y and en

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the form and function of pronominal verbs (e.g. se laver, se lever, se présenter), including the use of être and agreements when conjugating in the present perfect, for example, writing an email to a friend about what they did on a typical day last week

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using impersonal expressions such as il faut, on peut and on doit

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modal verbs (vouloir, pouvoir, devoir) to add complexity to spoken and written French, for example, writing the script for or participating in a conversation about what they must, should and want to do at home during the week

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the subjunctive (le subjonctif) verb forms in set, modelled phrases, for example, Il faut que tu partes; Il faut que je finisse mes devoirs

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E11 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the prepositions à and de in phrases, and being aware of the change of meaning with verbs that use both prepositions, for example, parler à quelqu’un vs. parler de quelque choses

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E12 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the gerund (le gérondif) as another method of talking about what occurred while something else was happening to show more complexity in their use of French, for example, Je suis tombé(e) en descendant l’escalier

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U03 - French
content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate French texts, using metalanguage to analyse language structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using metalanguage in English or French to identify the grammatical differences between languages or between their own first language and other languages they know, such as word order, verb moods and tenses, for example, the present perfect (le passé composé), possessive pronouns (les articles possessifs), agreements of adjectives and participles (l’accord des adjectifs et du participe passé), auxiliary verbs, and direct/indirect object pronouns

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing grammatical structures using metalanguage, for example, using relative clauses, relative pronouns and demonstrative adjectives to choose between qui, que and dont

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding when to use le passé composé and l’imparfait, comparing them with the equivalent terms in English

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing spoken and written texts such as apologies or invitations to identify how differences in grammar and text type determine the nature of formal and informal interactions, for example, Je t’invite ! Nous serions très heureux de vous accueillir chez nous

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how grammatical choices shade meaning and establish register, for example, the use of tu/vous to distinguish relationships; nous to suggest inclusivity or shared identity; on to suggest distance

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing sentence structures in French to English or other languages they know, and recognising the use of different clauses and tenses used to get the meaning across

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U03-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the use of personal pronouns, imperative/interrogative verb moods and emotive language in advertisements, identifying how grammatical choices, words and images combine in a text to achieve a particular purpose and effect

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U04 - French
content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the diversity of spoken forms of French from region to region (e.g. les accents du Midi; l’accent parisien, toulousain, picard) and between different French-speaking communities around the world (e.g. le Québec, La Réunion), considering how language variation can both reflect and shape social and cultural processes, with concepts such as la norme, la diversité, l’intelligibilité and les élites

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining to non-French speakers the expressions and cultural allusions encountered in French texts associated with historical, religious or civic events or traditions (e.g. la Marianne, le tricolore, la Toussaint, le 1er mai)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring intercultural communication, considering how their own cultural ways of thinking and behaving influence their own attitudes and other people’s responses or interpretations, and how attitudes can change over time

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering how the experience of learning a new language has had an impact on their awareness of their own communicative and cultural behaviours, and how these may be interpreted by others

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting gestures used by French speakers to signal meanings, such as Parfait ! and C’est fini, comparing these with gestures used in Australian English and other known languages, and using appropriate gestures when speaking French

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how language variation can reflect cultural and social identity, inclusion or exclusion, for example, reading speeches or advertisements and analysing the language used, identifying persuasive devices such as inclusive or emotive language

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the ways in which linguistic choices can vary to reflect diversity, for example, through the use of the point médian (e.g. un·e étudiant·e) and typical features of le langage épicène, such as non-gendered adjectives (e.g. aimable/sympa vs. gentil.le) and formulations (e.g. iel est une personne intéressante; iel est quelqu’un de patient)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing and discussing the interconnected nature of the linguistic and cultural diversity of French-speaking communities, and how this is also relevant to the linguistic and cultural diversity in Australia, including that of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U04-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and/or reading examples of an Acknowledgement of Country in French, and creating their own version that names the local Country for a French-speaking audience

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

as_extracts.name: LFREF1010-E04
as_extracts.description: They create texts, selecting and manipulating language for a range of contexts, purposes and audiences.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C03 - French
content_descriptions.text: interpret and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in a broad range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts and respond appropriately to context, purpose and audience
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: summarising information from spoken, written or visual texts that reflect different aspects of culture related to topics such as entertainment, special occasions, health and lifestyle or fashion

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing lyrics, themes and styles of popular French- and English-language songs, and tracking similarities and differences in ideas, referring to Eurovision or Victoires de la Musique / ARIA

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing extracts from expressive contemporary texts (e.g. tales, poems, songs, dance, street art, performances), including influences from minority groups and subcultures, and identifying and comparing elements of cultural traditions in Australia and the French-speaking world

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or reading an article or interview of a well-known Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander person, discussing their opinions and ideas in French, and creating and presenting their personal profile to the class

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: obtaining information from a range of viewed texts, including photographs, maps, illustrations and weather reports; using the ‘see, think, wonder’ thinking routine to identify and extract information; summarising the main points; and presenting the key information in their own words

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: summarising the key points from a range of texts such as social media and interviews

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying underlying values and cultural references in different texts, such as an advertisement or article, and evaluating their effect on audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C03-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining graphs, a table of statistics or pictures, and using the information gained from the texts to respond orally or in written form, for example, writing a formal letter to a member of parliament, requesting change based on evidence from the texts

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C04 - French
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to respond to non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and produce texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying vocabulary and expressions associated with particular elements of French lifestyles (e.g. la cuisine, la mode, les loisirs, la famille) in film or television clips, noting how the vocabulary changes according to audience and context, for example, les recettes de grands chefs / la cuisine en cinq minutes; la famille traditionnelle/recomposée … la belle mère / le beau père

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining information obtained from different sources to compare how young people are represented in the media (e.g. comparing letters to the editor about young people with blog posts written by young people), and responding in either oral or written form; for example, creating their own letter to the editor based on the opinions they have formed after obtaining information on the topic

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing short informative texts (e.g. documentary excerpts or news reports), and responding in written or oral form, for example, creating a speech to inform people about school stress or the dangers of climate change

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: conducting surveys or structured interviews with members of the class or online French-speaking contacts, comparing their opinions and perspectives on community or personal issues, identifying social or cultural variations, and reporting the findings back to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing excerpts from interviews with public figures (e.g. politicians, sports stars, musicians, actors), noting how vocabulary, phrases or gestures are used to emphasise or clarify key information, and collating a list of new phrases and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to popular French songs or viewing French music videos, summarising key ideas or messages, and comparing these with songs and music videos that appeal to young people in Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting cultural differences, protocols and conventions in genres such as selection criteria for job applications, lettre de motivation and formules de politesse, for example, responding to a job advertisement from a French website or newspaper

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting textual conventions popular with young French speakers, such as contractions, abbreviations and acronyms used in text messaging, for example, writing and responding to a series of text messages using acronyms such as bjr = bonjour, A+ = à plus, biz = bisous, and 12C4 = un de ces quatre

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C05 - French
content_descriptions.text: create and present texts for diverse contexts and purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and a range of textual conventions to engage different audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information in different text types (e.g. email, article, blog post, script of a speech) for different audiences (e.g. potential consumers, voters), identifying and using relevant textual conventions to create specific types of texts, using appropriate styles of writing (e.g. imaginative, informative, persuasive, personal, evaluative)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and illustrating a children’s storybook and reading it to younger children within the school or the community, using expressive French intonation, rhythm, pitch and appropriate gestures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading an instruction manual such as mode d’emploi pour l’installation d’un logiciel, and using plain French to rephrase the instructions for a partner to follow

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a journal entry or a contribution for a school newsletter in French, reflecting on a visit to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, and, with permission, referring to cultural knowledge of the site’s significance

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or travel brochure in French for travel to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do, traditional and/or cultural considerations, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and what to wear

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a letter to the council regarding an issue about the environment, for example, informing them about an environmental concern, evaluating a service or persuading them to improve a service to help the environment

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing artwork from a local Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander artist, and then writing a script of a speech to present to a group of French speakers introducing the artist

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a role-play using language for buying and selling goods and services, for example, ordering in a bakery; selling second-hand clothes; organising travel; considering the use of planes or trains to reduce their carbon footprint; raising money for charities

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: making language choices that indicate values and attitudes when creating texts, for example, the placement of nouns and adjectives in C’est un bon à rien; C’est un brave jeune homme / C’est un jeune homme brave; Ce sont des sans-papiers / Ce sont des réfugiés

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using emotive language and images when creating texts such as reports or speeches on current issues, for example, C’est émouvant; C’est troublant; C’est déraisonnable

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U01 - French
content_descriptions.text: apply features and conventions of spoken French to extend fluency, and to respond to and create a range of texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: increasing their fluency and accuracy in spoken French by using appropriate rhythm, pitch, intonation and liaisons, and adding in the extra t if needed

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using tone and intonation to indicate emphasis or emotion, for example, Elle a fait quoi ? Il est tellement doué !

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying correct pronunciation to more complex syllable combinations, for example, la magnitude les augmentations using sentence starters and connectors to increase the complexity of their responses, for example, Normalement je me lève à six heures du matin, mais ce matin, j’ai fait la grasse matinée et je me suis levé(e) à dix heures, car c’est le weekend !

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing discussion points in an argument by using sentence starters and connectors (e.g. premièrement deuxièmement ensuite de plus en revanche)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying appropriate pauses and pace of delivery to convey meaning, emphasis, feelings and emotion, and to create effects in spoken texts, for example, recording themselves presenting a speech or participating in a conversation, and reflecting on how they could improve or adjust the delivery of the information

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: adjusting the tone of spoken or written French to reflect the formality of the context, for example, using tu and vous correctly, and conjugating the accompanying verb

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to spontaneous questions from their teachers or peers on a range of topics, for example, answering questions such as Qu’est-ce que tu as fait pendant le weekend ? Qu’est-ce que tu vas faire ce weekend ? Pourquoi tu étudies le français ? Qu’est-ce que tu aimes faire normalement ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the fluid nature of spoken language, identifying features such as interactivity and the use of repetition, pauses and interruptions; contractions such as the dropping of ne in negative structures e.g. Je sais pas trop; incomplete sentences and reliance on non-verbal elements and vocal expression such as Dis donc, t’es là ? Je suis déjà là – t’es où, toi ?

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U02 - French
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to predict meaning, and to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how grammatical choices indicate meaning, determine perspective and establish relationships, for example, how imperative verbs are used to show authority or enthusiasm, Arrêtez !; Allons-y !; Donnez-moi votre billet, Mademoiselle

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the comparative and superlative forms of adverbs and adjectives (e.g. plus vite / le plus vite; moins jolie / la moins jolie; meilleur / le meilleur), for example, reading a text and highlighting the positive, comparative and superlative adjectives in different colours, before creating a table that reflects each adjective in the different forms, and then playing a speaking game where each person adapts the sentence before by changing the adjective

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using multiple tenses (e.g. le présent, le futur proche, le futur, le passé composé, l’imparfait) and le conditionnel in both written and spoken French, for example, writing a series of short diary entries about a holiday, including details about what they did during a previous day, what their family is doing now and what they are planning to do on an upcoming day

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that verbs conjugated in the present perfect (le passé composé) with the auxiliary être (intransitive verbs, pronominal verbs and passive voice) require agreement of the past participle with the subject (e.g. Elles sont parties hier soir; Je me suis levée à sept heures; Nous nous sommes amusés; La pomme a été mangée par Pierre), as do verbs conjugated in the present perfect with the auxiliary verb avoir when preceded by the direct object pronoun (e.g. J’ai acheté des fleurs, et je les ai données à ma mère)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the imperfect (l’imparfait), and understanding how to distinguish between a completed and a continuing action in the past, for example, Nous étions déjà au lit quand il est arrivé

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the use of relative pronouns (qui, que), emphatic pronouns (e.g. moi, elle, eux), and direct and indirect object pronouns (le, la, lui, nous, vous, les, leur), and having exposure to y and en

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the form and function of pronominal verbs (e.g. se laver, se lever, se présenter), including the use of être and agreements when conjugating in the present perfect, for example, writing an email to a friend about what they did on a typical day last week

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using impersonal expressions such as il faut, on peut and on doit

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modal verbs (vouloir, pouvoir, devoir) to add complexity to spoken and written French, for example, writing the script for or participating in a conversation about what they must, should and want to do at home during the week

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the subjunctive (le subjonctif) verb forms in set, modelled phrases, for example, Il faut que tu partes; Il faut que je finisse mes devoirs

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E11 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the prepositions à and de in phrases, and being aware of the change of meaning with verbs that use both prepositions, for example, parler à quelqu’un vs. parler de quelque choses

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E12 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the gerund (le gérondif) as another method of talking about what occurred while something else was happening to show more complexity in their use of French, for example, Je suis tombé(e) en descendant l’escalier

as_extracts.name: LFREF1010-E05
as_extracts.description: They apply and use complex sentences and structures to create and respond to spoken and written texts.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C01 - French
content_descriptions.text: initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts related to their own and others’ experiences of the world, adjusting their language in response to others

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating and sustaining conversation by introducing topics, inviting contributions or asking for clarification, for example, Qu’est-ce que vous en pensez ?; Je n’ai pas bien compris …; Si on parlait de …?

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating and sustaining exchanges with others by acknowledging, asking and expanding questions, making excuses and apologising, using forms of politeness and respect, for example, Pouvez-vous parler plus lentement, s’il vous plaît ?; Je n’ai pas compris.; J’ai oublié.; Je ne me souviens pas.; Je vous en prie.; Pourriez-vous m’excuser ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in discussions about young people in French-speaking contexts, sharing aspects of school and home life (e.g. le stress, le sport, l’étude des langues, les droits, les tâches ménagères, la vie quotidienne, habiter à la campagne ou en ville, les responsabilités civiques)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining or justifying a position in relation to personal and social issues (e.g. les études, la santé, l’avenir, les passe-temps)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: building topic-specific vocabulary and rhetorical strategies such as emphasis and repetition, for example, Au contraire ! À mon avis …; Je ne suis pas d’accord.; Après tout …; Il faut le dire …; Encore une fois …

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using descriptive and expressive language to exchange views on global issues (e.g. la diversité, le changement climatique, les médias sociaux, l’avenir des jeunes, la pollution)

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV2
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews are formed by different experiences at a personal, local, national and global level, and are linked to individual, community and political mandates and actions for sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: building fluency in speech by responding to sets of questions on familiar topics over multiple occasions, each time either adding more content into their response or adding sentence starters and connecters (e.g. normalement, de plus, en fait, en effet)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled strategies and phrases to allow thinking time to help formulate their responses to spontaneous questions, for example, repeating the question aloud and using phrases such as C’est une bonne question, qu’est-ce que j’en pense ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using strategies to sustain interactions such as asking for clarification or confirmation, or providing suggestions, for example, Vraiment ? / C’est vrai ?; Pardon ?; Comment ?; Quand ?; Avec qui ?; Pourquoi ?; Vous disiez ?; Qu’est-ce que tu veux dire ?; Tu as raison ! Je suis d’accord.; Que penses-tu ? Je te conseille de …; Selon moi, c’est une idée géniale.

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: accepting an invitation, or responding with reasons for declining or negotiating alternative arrangements, adjusting language to suit formal or informal contexts, for example, Je suis ravi(e) de vous rencontrer / d’accepter l’invitation à la fête. Désolé(e) mais je dois dire non … C’est dommage.; Ça te va dimanche ? Je ne peux pas samedi. Malheureusement …

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C02 - French
content_descriptions.text: contribute to discussions that involve diverse views to negotiate outcomes, address issues and compare experiences

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital communication (e.g. email, group chats, SMS, texts, community websites), implementing safe and ethical protocols, including responsible engagement with the audience, to plan real or imaged events or activities such as la Fête de la Musique or cahier/guide de recommandations pour visiter un pays francophone

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising real or simulated forums, to raise awareness of environmental, social or ethical issues (e.g. le réchauffement climatique; les droits des populations indigènes; le développement durable; les préjugés; la discrimination)

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV2
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews are formed by different experiences at a personal, local, national and global level, and are linked to individual, community and political mandates and actions for sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a news segment, for school or a community television or radio station, using appropriate terms to introduce, identify and summarise, for example, En direct de …; Notre envoyé spécial …; L’enquête de …; Les titres / en tête / à la une de cette édition …

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating for goods and services, considering concepts of value for money, availability, competition and ethics of production

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSRD1
organising_ideas.text: Responsibly designed products and services aim to minimise the human impact on the environment and restore the quality, ecological integrity and diversity of economic, social, environmental and cultural systems.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising and planning an occasion, for example, Si on allait au théâtre ? Non, le théâtre ne m’intéresse pas. Je préfère aller …; On se trouve à …; Rendez-vous à la gare.; On arrive à 18h chez mon frère.

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: preparing print or digital information for real or imagined French visitors to the school, for example, recording/filming an introduction to the school, preparing welcome speeches, or conducting guided tours of the school

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C02-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating the elements of an ideal home with team members (e.g. how many bedrooms, types of shared spaces, outdoor areas, number of bathrooms) and using digital tools to design it, for example, Moi, je voudrais un jardin immense; Ah moi, je préfère une salle de bains à moi

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C02-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a news clip or part of an informative video and using what was introduced in the clip as a prompt for discussion, starting with summarising, and then providing their own opinion and justifying this opinion

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C05 - French
content_descriptions.text: create and present texts for diverse contexts and purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and a range of textual conventions to engage different audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information in different text types (e.g. email, article, blog post, script of a speech) for different audiences (e.g. potential consumers, voters), identifying and using relevant textual conventions to create specific types of texts, using appropriate styles of writing (e.g. imaginative, informative, persuasive, personal, evaluative)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and illustrating a children’s storybook and reading it to younger children within the school or the community, using expressive French intonation, rhythm, pitch and appropriate gestures

elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or travel brochure in French for travel to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do, traditional and/or cultural considerations, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and what to wear

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a letter to the council regarding an issue about the environment, for example, informing them about an environmental concern, evaluating a service or persuading them to improve a service to help the environment

organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing artwork from a local Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander artist, and then writing a script of a speech to present to a group of French speakers introducing the artist

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a role-play using language for buying and selling goods and services, for example, ordering in a bakery; selling second-hand clothes; organising travel; considering the use of planes or trains to reduce their carbon footprint; raising money for charities

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: making language choices that indicate values and attitudes when creating texts, for example, the placement of nouns and adjectives in C’est un bon à rien; C’est un brave jeune homme / C’est un jeune homme brave; Ce sont des sans-papiers / Ce sont des réfugiés

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using emotive language and images when creating texts such as reports or speeches on current issues, for example, C’est émouvant; C’est troublant; C’est déraisonnable

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U01 - French
content_descriptions.text: apply features and conventions of spoken French to extend fluency, and to respond to and create a range of texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: increasing their fluency and accuracy in spoken French by using appropriate rhythm, pitch, intonation and liaisons, and adding in the extra t if needed

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using tone and intonation to indicate emphasis or emotion, for example, Elle a fait quoi ? Il est tellement doué !

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying correct pronunciation to more complex syllable combinations, for example, la magnitude les augmentations using sentence starters and connectors to increase the complexity of their responses, for example, Normalement je me lève à six heures du matin, mais ce matin, j’ai fait la grasse matinée et je me suis levé(e) à dix heures, car c’est le weekend !

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing discussion points in an argument by using sentence starters and connectors (e.g. premièrement deuxièmement ensuite de plus en revanche)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying appropriate pauses and pace of delivery to convey meaning, emphasis, feelings and emotion, and to create effects in spoken texts, for example, recording themselves presenting a speech or participating in a conversation, and reflecting on how they could improve or adjust the delivery of the information

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: adjusting the tone of spoken or written French to reflect the formality of the context, for example, using tu and vous correctly, and conjugating the accompanying verb

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to spontaneous questions from their teachers or peers on a range of topics, for example, answering questions such as Qu’est-ce que tu as fait pendant le weekend ? Qu’est-ce que tu vas faire ce weekend ? Pourquoi tu étudies le français ? Qu’est-ce que tu aimes faire normalement ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U01-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the fluid nature of spoken language, identifying features such as interactivity and the use of repetition, pauses and interruptions; contractions such as the dropping of ne in negative structures e.g. Je sais pas trop; incomplete sentences and reliance on non-verbal elements and vocal expression such as Dis donc, t’es là ? Je suis déjà là – t’es où, toi ?

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10U02 - French
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to predict meaning, and to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how grammatical choices indicate meaning, determine perspective and establish relationships, for example, how imperative verbs are used to show authority or enthusiasm, Arrêtez !; Allons-y !; Donnez-moi votre billet, Mademoiselle

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the comparative and superlative forms of adverbs and adjectives (e.g. plus vite / le plus vite; moins jolie / la moins jolie; meilleur / le meilleur), for example, reading a text and highlighting the positive, comparative and superlative adjectives in different colours, before creating a table that reflects each adjective in the different forms, and then playing a speaking game where each person adapts the sentence before by changing the adjective

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using multiple tenses (e.g. le présent, le futur proche, le futur, le passé composé, l’imparfait) and le conditionnel in both written and spoken French, for example, writing a series of short diary entries about a holiday, including details about what they did during a previous day, what their family is doing now and what they are planning to do on an upcoming day

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that verbs conjugated in the present perfect (le passé composé) with the auxiliary être (intransitive verbs, pronominal verbs and passive voice) require agreement of the past participle with the subject (e.g. Elles sont parties hier soir; Je me suis levée à sept heures; Nous nous sommes amusés; La pomme a été mangée par Pierre), as do verbs conjugated in the present perfect with the auxiliary verb avoir when preceded by the direct object pronoun (e.g. J’ai acheté des fleurs, et je les ai données à ma mère)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the imperfect (l’imparfait), and understanding how to distinguish between a completed and a continuing action in the past, for example, Nous étions déjà au lit quand il est arrivé

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the use of relative pronouns (qui, que), emphatic pronouns (e.g. moi, elle, eux), and direct and indirect object pronouns (le, la, lui, nous, vous, les, leur), and having exposure to y and en

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the form and function of pronominal verbs (e.g. se laver, se lever, se présenter), including the use of être and agreements when conjugating in the present perfect, for example, writing an email to a friend about what they did on a typical day last week

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using impersonal expressions such as il faut, on peut and on doit

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modal verbs (vouloir, pouvoir, devoir) to add complexity to spoken and written French, for example, writing the script for or participating in a conversation about what they must, should and want to do at home during the week

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the subjunctive (le subjonctif) verb forms in set, modelled phrases, for example, Il faut que tu partes; Il faut que je finisse mes devoirs

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E11 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the prepositions à and de in phrases, and being aware of the change of meaning with verbs that use both prepositions, for example, parler à quelqu’un vs. parler de quelque choses

elaborations.name: VC2LF10U02-E12 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the gerund (le gérondif) as another method of talking about what occurred while something else was happening to show more complexity in their use of French, for example, Je suis tombé(e) en descendant l’escalier

as_extracts.name: LFREF1010-E06
as_extracts.description: They use a variety of tenses to sequence events and use language structures and features to enhance meaning and cohesion.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C04 - French
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to respond to non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and produce texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying vocabulary and expressions associated with particular elements of French lifestyles (e.g. la cuisine, la mode, les loisirs, la famille) in film or television clips, noting how the vocabulary changes according to audience and context, for example, les recettes de grands chefs / la cuisine en cinq minutes; la famille traditionnelle/recomposée … la belle mère / le beau père

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining information obtained from different sources to compare how young people are represented in the media (e.g. comparing letters to the editor about young people with blog posts written by young people), and responding in either oral or written form; for example, creating their own letter to the editor based on the opinions they have formed after obtaining information on the topic

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing short informative texts (e.g. documentary excerpts or news reports), and responding in written or oral form, for example, creating a speech to inform people about school stress or the dangers of climate change

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.

elaborations.elaboration_text: conducting surveys or structured interviews with members of the class or online French-speaking contacts, comparing their opinions and perspectives on community or personal issues, identifying social or cultural variations, and reporting the findings back to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing excerpts from interviews with public figures (e.g. politicians, sports stars, musicians, actors), noting how vocabulary, phrases or gestures are used to emphasise or clarify key information, and collating a list of new phrases and expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to popular French songs or viewing French music videos, summarising key ideas or messages, and comparing these with songs and music videos that appeal to young people in Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting cultural differences, protocols and conventions in genres such as selection criteria for job applications, lettre de motivation and formules de politesse, for example, responding to a job advertisement from a French website or newspaper

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C04-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting textual conventions popular with young French speakers, such as contractions, abbreviations and acronyms used in text messaging, for example, writing and responding to a series of text messages using acronyms such as bjr = bonjour, A+ = à plus, biz = bisous, and 12C4 = un de ces quatre

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C01 - French
content_descriptions.text: initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts related to their own and others’ experiences of the world, adjusting their language in response to others

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating and sustaining conversation by introducing topics, inviting contributions or asking for clarification, for example, Qu’est-ce que vous en pensez ?; Je n’ai pas bien compris …; Si on parlait de …?

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating and sustaining exchanges with others by acknowledging, asking and expanding questions, making excuses and apologising, using forms of politeness and respect, for example, Pouvez-vous parler plus lentement, s’il vous plaît ?; Je n’ai pas compris.; J’ai oublié.; Je ne me souviens pas.; Je vous en prie.; Pourriez-vous m’excuser ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in discussions about young people in French-speaking contexts, sharing aspects of school and home life (e.g. le stress, le sport, l’étude des langues, les droits, les tâches ménagères, la vie quotidienne, habiter à la campagne ou en ville, les responsabilités civiques)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining or justifying a position in relation to personal and social issues (e.g. les études, la santé, l’avenir, les passe-temps)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: building topic-specific vocabulary and rhetorical strategies such as emphasis and repetition, for example, Au contraire ! À mon avis …; Je ne suis pas d’accord.; Après tout …; Il faut le dire …; Encore une fois …

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using descriptive and expressive language to exchange views on global issues (e.g. la diversité, le changement climatique, les médias sociaux, l’avenir des jeunes, la pollution)

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV2
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews are formed by different experiences at a personal, local, national and global level, and are linked to individual, community and political mandates and actions for sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E07 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: building fluency in speech by responding to sets of questions on familiar topics over multiple occasions, each time either adding more content into their response or adding sentence starters and connecters (e.g. normalement, de plus, en fait, en effet)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E08 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled strategies and phrases to allow thinking time to help formulate their responses to spontaneous questions, for example, repeating the question aloud and using phrases such as C’est une bonne question, qu’est-ce que j’en pense ?

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E09 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: using strategies to sustain interactions such as asking for clarification or confirmation, or providing suggestions, for example, Vraiment ? / C’est vrai ?; Pardon ?; Comment ?; Quand ?; Avec qui ?; Pourquoi ?; Vous disiez ?; Qu’est-ce que tu veux dire ?; Tu as raison ! Je suis d’accord.; Que penses-tu ? Je te conseille de …; Selon moi, c’est une idée géniale.

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C01-E10 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: accepting an invitation, or responding with reasons for declining or negotiating alternative arrangements, adjusting language to suit formal or informal contexts, for example, Je suis ravi(e) de vous rencontrer / d’accepter l’invitation à la fête. Désolé(e) mais je dois dire non … C’est dommage.; Ça te va dimanche ? Je ne peux pas samedi. Malheureusement …

content_descriptions.name: VC2LF10C05 - French
content_descriptions.text: create and present texts for diverse contexts and purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and a range of textual conventions to engage different audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E01 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information in different text types (e.g. email, article, blog post, script of a speech) for different audiences (e.g. potential consumers, voters), identifying and using relevant textual conventions to create specific types of texts, using appropriate styles of writing (e.g. imaginative, informative, persuasive, personal, evaluative)

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E02 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and illustrating a children’s storybook and reading it to younger children within the school or the community, using expressive French intonation, rhythm, pitch and appropriate gestures

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E03 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading an instruction manual such as mode d’emploi pour l’installation d’un logiciel, and using plain French to rephrase the instructions for a partner to follow

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E04 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a journal entry or a contribution for a school newsletter in French, reflecting on a visit to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, and, with permission, referring to cultural knowledge of the site’s significance

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E05 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or travel brochure in French for travel to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do, traditional and/or cultural considerations, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and what to wear

elaborations.name: VC2LF10C05-E06 - French
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a letter to the council regarding an issue about the environment, for example, informing them about an environmental concern, evaluating a service or persuading them to improve a service to help the environment

elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing artwork from a local Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander artist, and then writing a script of a speech to present to a group of French speakers introducing the artist

organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
